title: Complete assembly of the canonical point realization specification
statement: Fix the finite-field datum D, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with integer ring $\mathcal O_E$, as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The seven-property proposition pointTransportTowerRealizationSpec of [def-trf-point-transport-tower-realization-specification] holds. Its witnesses are the natural strict finite map, actual quotient augmentation and normalized sectionwise target Roos isomorphism of [lem-trf-point-transport-tower-natural-constructions]. Thus no unspecified comparison or arbitrary finite reduction realization is substituted for the stated data.

source.place: clause *(3)*: the integral point transport is the derived limit of the levelwise maps, via its specified cone map; implementation module PointTransportTowerRealizationAssembly

proof.text: Unfold the seven-property specification and choose the constructed U, alpha and beta. The finite component formula follows from the all-complex finite law; the first augmentation coordinate follows from the existing quotient-unit section formula.

Use the whole shifted-coordinate equality for alpha. Both beta coordinate equations are the two existing sectionwise Roos comparison projections, after unfolding the explicitly typed target endomorphisms.

For a good constructible representative apply actual-quotient augmentation invertibility. The strict good-representative augmentation square supplies the hypothesis of the derived identity lemma. Its conclusion proves the exact specified integral transport realization equation.
The existing derived natural transformation gives the final naturality clause for every derived morphism.

proof_origin.place: clause *(3)*: the integral point transport is the derived limit of the levelwise maps, via its specified cone map; implementation module PointTransportTowerRealizationAssembly

mathlib_searches.query: exact evaluation of inverse towers commutes with the two-coordinate Roos mapping cocone, natural quotient augmentation, and finite Frobenius point transport
mathlib_searches.results: Generic limits and cocone comparison equations, tensor quotient maps, and inverse Frobenius on perfect rings; no coefficient-sheaf point construction. Existing project constructions are reused.
Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.MappingCocone: mappingCocone, fst, snd, liftCochain and projection equations. These are the generic ingredients, not the specified integral point data.
Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.OfSequence supplies ofOpSequence and NatTrans.ofOpSequence. No specialized realization or finite point iterate; source constructions already exist in Sheaf.
mathlib_searches.verdict: no exact Mathlib match; reuse the project API
